headline: Every segment grows as capital return stays disciplined
summary_short: Voya's Q1 2026 revenue was $2,031M (+3.1% y/y, roughly flat q/q) as GAAP diluted EPS reached $1.75 (+23.2% y/y) and after-tax adjusted operating EPS hit $2.26 (+13% y/y), with all three segments — Retirement, Investment Management, and Employee Benefits — posting higher pre-tax adjusted operating earnings.
summary_long: Revenue rose 3.1% y/y on fee income (+$34M, higher equity markets and Retirement/Investment Management momentum) and net investment income (+$9M, LP valuations, fixed-income yield actions), partly offset by wider net investment losses. Adjusted operating earnings reached $214M ($2.26/share, +13% y/y): Investment Management +12% on fee growth, Employee Benefits +37% on underwriting and fee income, Retirement roughly flat. The company generated ~$200M of excess capital, returned $150M via buybacks plus $44M in dividends, and agreed to a further $150M buyback in Q2 2026. Long-term debt rose to $2,500M on a $400M issuance for Senior Notes maturing June 2026; equity fell to $4,658M on a comprehensive loss plus buybacks/dividends. RBC ratio was 396%, pro forma excess capital ~$0.25B.

drivers.explanation: All three segments — Retirement, Investment Management, Employee Benefits — posted higher pre-tax adjusted operating earnings; Investment Management +12% on fee growth, Employee Benefits +37% on underwriting and fee income.
Fee income +$34M on higher average equity markets and Retirement/Investment Management commercial momentum; net investment income +$9M on LP valuations and fixed-income yield actions.
Diluted EPS growth driven by higher after-tax adjusted operating earnings, lower losses on businesses exited, and lower acquisition-integration costs.
Same drivers as net income (higher adjusted operating earnings, lower exited-business losses, lower integration costs), plus a smaller diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.
Tracks the net income increase; basic and diluted differ only by the dilutive effect of equity awards.
Tracks the net income increase; income tax expense rose to $35M from $22M as the effective rate increased to 15.2% from 12.7%.
Cash fell q/q as $150M of buybacks, $44M of dividends, and a $129M contingent-consideration payment to OneAmerica outweighed the $400M debt issuance and operating/investing inflows.
Debt rose on a $400M issuance earmarked to repay the 3.65% Senior Notes maturing June 15, 2026.
Equity fell q/q as the quarter's $(91)M comprehensive loss (unfavorable AOCI) combined with $151M of share buybacks and $61M of preferred-plus-common dividends recorded in equity.
Share count fell on ongoing buybacks: $150M repurchased this quarter, plus a further $150M agreed for Q2 2026.
